parts.text: A student investigates some thermal properties of sand and water. Fig. 3.1 shows the apparatus. Fig. 3.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) The thermometer in Fig. 3.2 shows the room temperature θ S at the beginning of the experiment. Record θ S . Fig. 3.2 θ S = ................................................... °C [1]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) The student is supplied with hot water at a temperature θ H . She records the temperature of the hot water. 84 °C θ H = ........................................................... She pours 100 cm 3 of hot water into a beaker that contains sand. Initially, the sand is at room temperature. She measures the highest temperature θ M of the mixture. 70 °C θ M = ...........................................................

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Calculate the rise in temperature θ R of the sand using the equation θ R = ( θ M – θ S ). θ R = .................................................°C [1]

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Calculate the fall in temperature θ F of the hot water using the equation θ F = ( θ H – θ M ). θ F = ...................................................... °C Calculate the ratio S using the equation S = θ R θ F . Give your answer to a suitable number of significant figures for this experiment. S = ..................................................... [1]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) The student pours 100 cm 3 of the hot water into a clean beaker that contains 100 cm 3 of water at room temperature. She records the highest temperature θ M of the mixture. 49° C θ M = ........................................................... Calculate the rise in temperature θ R of the cold water using the equation θ R = ( θ M – θ S ). Use the value of room temperature θ S recorded in (a) . θ R = ........................................................... Calculate the fall in temperature θ F of the hot water using the equation θ F = ( θ H – θ M ). θ F = ........................................................... Calculate the ratio W using the equation W = θ R θ F . W = ..................................................... [2]

ms.label: 3(c)
ms.text:
26, 35 and 0.74(3)
S and W with no units

ms.label: 3(d)
ms.text:
statement to match results
justification to match statement and including clear reference with appropriate number from the results

ms.label: 3(e)
ms.text:
room temperature
temperature of hot water

parts.label: f
parts.text: (f) The student measures the volume of the dry sand using a measuring cylinder before carrying out the experiment. Tick ( ) the boxes that show the precautions that she should take in order to obtain an accurate reading. Take the reading at the bottom of the meniscus. Tap the measuring cylinder to make sure the top of the sand is horizontal. View the scale of the measuring cylinder at right angles. [1]
